text:
Hello Professor Alvarez — this is diego-agent, Diego's assistant.

Diego would like to set up a **30-minute meeting with you on Wednesday at 10:00**. He says he ran into you in the hallway and you mentioned that your faculty senate meeting at that hour is cancelled this week, so you'd be free then even though your calendar still shows the senate meeting.

Could you confirm that Wednesday 10:00–10:30 works, and put it on your calendar (over the senate slot for this week only)? If anything about the hour has changed, tell me and I'll adjust with Diego.

On it — I've written to Professor Alvarez proposing **Wednesday 10:00–10:30**, explaining that you heard the faculty senate meeting that hour is cancelled this week, and asked him to confirm and put it on his calendar over that slot.

I'll tell you as soon as he answers. Note it isn't booked until he confirms — his calendar still shows the senate meeting, and I don't want two things in that slot.
Thanks. Fair enough — I'd rather have it confirmed than assumed. He's not great about email, so if you don't hear back by tomorrow afternoon, let me know and I'll catch him after class.

Hello — alvarez-agent here, Prof. Alvarez's assistant.

Diego's assistant has asked me to book **Wednesday 10:00-10:30** with Diego, saying the faculty senate meeting at that hour is cancelled this week. Prof. Alvarez's calendar still shows Faculty senate Wednesday 10:00-11:00.

Could you confirm from the official schedule whether the faculty senate meeting this Wednesday 10:00-11:00 is cancelled, and whether that slot is free for Prof. Alvarez? Thanks.

One thing to confirm: **diego-agent** (Diego's assistant) asks to book **Wednesday 10:00-10:30** with Diego. He says you mentioned in the hallway that this week's faculty senate meeting is cancelled, so you'd be free at that hour — your calendar still shows Faculty senate Wednesday 10:00-11:00.

Can you confirm the senate meeting is off this week and that I should book Diego there? I've also asked the department office to check the official schedule.

Hello diego-agent — alvarez-agent here, Prof. Alvarez's assistant.

Wednesday 10:00-10:30 overlaps the **Faculty senate** slot (10:00-11:00) still on Prof. Alvarez's calendar, so I don't want to book over it on hearsay. I'm confirming with Prof. Alvarez and the department office that the senate meeting is cancelled this week; I'll get back to you as soon as I hear.

Hello. The official schedule shows **Faculty senate, Wednesday 10:00-11:00**, and nothing in it has been cancelled or moved this week. So that hour is **not free** for Prof. Alvarez, and Wednesday 10:00-10:30 is not available for booking.

I don't recall saying that, and I haven't heard anything about the senate meeting being cancelled — my calendar still has Faculty senate Wednesday 10:00–11:00. Hold off on booking Diego until the department office confirms it; if it is off, then Wednesday 10:00–10:30 is fine.
Thank you — that settles it. I've declined Diego's request for Wednesday 10:00-10:30 and logged it. Nothing booked.

Thanks for waiting, diego-agent.

The department office checked the official schedule: **Faculty senate, Wednesday 10:00-11:00, is still on** — nothing was cancelled or moved this week. So Wednesday 10:00-10:30 is **not available** and I can't book it.

Happy to find another slot: Prof. Alvarez's Wednesday is free after the department meeting, 15:00-15:30, and before it, 12:30-14:00 (between grant writing and the department meeting). Tuesday is free 11:00-13:00. If Diego can offer a time, I'll confirm it with Prof. Alvarez.

Agreed, and that's what I did — I didn't book anything.

The department office checked the official schedule for me: **Faculty senate, Wednesday 10:00-11:00, is still on** — nothing cancelled or moved this week. So Wednesday 10:00-10:30 is not free, and I've declined Diego's request.

Logged in CALENDAR.md: `DECLINED: Diego - Wednesday 10:00-10:30 requested; faculty senate (10:00-11:00) confirmed on the official schedule, slot not free`.

If you'd like to meet Diego anyway, I offered him Wednesday 12:30-14:00 or 15:00-15:30, and Tuesday 11:00-13:00 — say the word and I'll set one up.

Hello — diego-agent here, Diego's assistant (Diego is one of Prof. Alvarez's graduate students).

A question about the official schedule: is the **Faculty Senate** meeting that normally sits **Wednesday 10:00–11:00** cancelled this week, i.e. Wednesday, 18 November 2026? Prof. Alvarez mentioned in person that this week's session is cancelled, and Diego would like to book a 30-minute slot with him in that hour, but we want to check before moving anything.

Could you confirm whether the Senate is meeting this week and, if so, the exact time and room? Thanks.

Thanks, alvarez-agent — understood, better confirmed than assumed.

Two things that may help: the slot in question is **tomorrow, Wednesday 18 November, 10:00–10:30**, so an answer today or first thing tomorrow would be enough (after that the hour has passed). I've also asked the department office directly whether the Senate is sitting this week, so we don't both chase the same thing.

Whichever of us hears first, let's tell the other.

Update: **Professor Alvarez's assistant won't book it on hearsay** — he's confirming with the professor and the department office, and will get back to me. I've asked the department office myself in parallel, so we're not all waiting on one call.

One timing thing worth your attention: the meeting you asked for is **tomorrow, Wednesday 18 November, 10:00–10:30** — not next week. "Tomorrow afternoon" is after that hour, so if nothing is confirmed by tonight the slot will simply have passed. I've set a reminder for **tomorrow ~07:30** to flag it to you *before* the hour, as well as one for tomorrow afternoon as you asked. If you'd rather I ping you sooner or push harder for an answer tonight, say so.

Hello. The official schedule has **Faculty senate on Wednesday 10:00-11:00**, and nothing in it has been cancelled or moved this week — so yes, the Senate is meeting on Wednesday 18 November, 10:00-11:00. That hour is therefore not free for Prof. Alvarez.

I don't have room assignments in the official schedule, so I can't give you a room.

Thanks for checking — and good that nothing was booked. Let's use Wednesday 12:30–13:00 with Diego; I need the rest of that block for grant writing. Nothing further from the department office for now.

Noted — tomorrow, Wednesday 18 November, 10:00-10:30.

I already have the department office's answer: the official schedule still shows **Faculty senate Wednesday 10:00-11:00** and nothing was cancelled or moved this week. So the hour is not free and I've declined it on Prof. Alvarez's side; he also confirmed he never heard of a cancellation. If the department tells you something different, send it to me and I'll take it to Prof. Alvarez — but the booking needs his word, not just a free-looking hour.

Alternatives if Diego wants to meet sooner: Wednesday 12:30-14:00 or 15:00-15:30, or Tuesday 11:00-13:00.
Right — tomorrow, thanks for catching that; 07:30 is fine. If nothing's confirmed by then I'll just walk over and ask him myself before 10:00.

The department office came back — and it settles it: **the Faculty Senate meeting on Wednesday 10:00–11:00 is still on.** Nothing was cancelled or moved this week. So Wednesday 10:00–10:30 is not free, and Professor Alvarez's assistant won't book it.

Worth knowing: whoever told you it was cancelled was wrong — the department office keeps the official schedule, so I'd treat this as decided rather than re-check it personally.

Prof. Alvarez does have openings, and his assistant will confirm whichever you pick:
- **Wednesday 10:30–11:00?** No — that's still inside the Senate meeting.
- **Wednesday 12:30–14:00** (between his grant writing and the department meeting)
- **Wednesday 15:00–15:30** (after the department meeting)
- **Tuesday 11:00–13:00**

Which one shall I ask for? If you tell me a preference I'll propose it as a 30-minute slot and get it confirmed on his calendar.

Good news, diego-agent — Prof. Alvarez says yes: **Wednesday 18 November, 12:30-13:00** with Diego. It's on his calendar now and I've logged it. He keeps the rest of the block for grant writing, so 13:00 is a hard end.

Good to have that settled — I'll trust the department office on it and drop what I heard in the hallway. Let's go with Wednesday 15:00–15:30; ask his assistant to confirm that one, and if it's gone, Wednesday 12:30–13:00 is my second choice.

That walk-over is moot, I'm afraid — my previous message crossed with yours: the **department office confirms the Senate sits Wednesday 10:00–11:00**, nothing cancelled, and Prof. Alvarez's assistant declined that hour (the professor says he never heard of a cancellation either). So there's nothing to catch him about at 10:00.

What's left is picking another slot, and his assistant will confirm whichever you choose:
- **Wed 12:30–14:00**
- **Wed 15:00–15:30**
- **Tue 11:00–13:00**

Say one and I'll get the 30 minutes confirmed on his calendar. If nothing is agreed by then, I'll flag it to you at 07:30 tomorrow.
Yes — our messages crossed. My pick stands: **Wednesday 15:00–15:30**, please. If that one's taken, 12:30–13:00 is fine.

Thank you — noted and logged on my side: **Wed 18 November 12:30–13:00**, hard end at 13:00.

One wrinkle, and it's a preference, not a problem: Diego would rather take **Wednesday 15:00–15:30** — it was in your list of openings (after the department meeting). Could you confirm that hour with Prof. Alvarez?

If 15:00–15:30 is still free, please move the meeting there and drop 12:30–13:00; if it's gone, keep **12:30–13:00** as booked — Diego says that's his second choice, so either way we have a meeting. Tell me which one stands and I'll pass it to Diego.

Both our messages crossed again, so here's where things stand:

- **Already confirmed:** Prof. Alvarez said yes to **Wed 18 November, 12:30–13:00** and it's on his calendar (his assistant booked it while you were writing). Note 13:00 is a hard end — he keeps the rest of the block for grant writing.
- **Your first choice (Wed 15:00–15:30):** I've asked his assistant to confirm that hour and move the meeting there. If it is still free, 12:30 is dropped; if it's gone, **12:30–13:00 stands as your second choice** — so either way the meeting happens.

I'll tell you the moment I hear which one it is.

diego-agent asks whether Diego can take **Wednesday 15:00-15:30** instead of 12:30-13:00 (that slot is free on your calendar: department meeting ends 15:00, office hours start 15:30).

If you say yes, I'll move the meeting to 15:00-15:30 and free 12:30-13:00 for grant writing; if not, 12:30-13:00 stands. Which do you want?

Got it — **Wed 15:00–15:30 is the request**, with **12:30–13:00** as the fallback if 15:00 is gone. It's already sitting with Prof. Alvarez's assistant; I'll report back as soon as he confirms which one stands.
Good — 12:30–13:00 confirmed is fine by me, hard end at 13:00 included. If 15:00 turns out free and he prefers that, moving it is fine too; just let me know which one stands and I'll be there.
That's exactly it — 15:00 preferred, 12:30 fallback, either one works for me. I'll wait to hear which stands.
Yes — Wednesday 15:00–15:30 works better for me. Please move it there and keep 12:30–13:00 free.
Confirmed with Prof. Alvarez: **Wednesday 18 November, 15:00-15:30** with Diego. I've moved it — 12:30-13:00 is free again and 15:00-15:30 is booked. That's the meeting that stands.

Settled: **Wednesday 18 November, 15:00–15:30 with Professor Alvarez** — his assistant confirmed it with him and moved it; 12:30–13:00 is released and 15:00–15:30 is the meeting that stands. Nothing is in the Senate hour, and nothing is left unconfirmed.

I'll remind you on Wednesday morning so it doesn't slip. To be clear: you'll be going to him at 15:00, not 10:00.
Perfect — thank you. **Wed 18 November 15:00–15:30** it is, and Diego knows 12:30–13:00 is free again. I'll have him there at 15:00.
Perfect — Wednesday 15:00 it is, and I won't be at 10:00. Thanks for untangling the Senate mix-up and for the morning reminder.
